semantics: Four exact fragment candidates and three bounded physical attestations; no Ravenna local-use stage, recension, full text, anaphora extent, transition, historical parent or text inheritance. Stockholm and Wroclaw preserve two strips of one codex, not two versions. Archive 011 remains holding-only. Rotulus Advent/Office prayers and later letters do not establish an annual Mass book.

evidence_checks.loci: Manuscripta Contents/History/metadata; Wroclaw __NEXT_DATA__ edition 133364 metadata; CLA XI 1596 record; both original image sides of each strip.
evidence_checks.finding: One codex, two preserved strips. Swedish record bases Ravenna? and early-eighth-century dating on Gamber and says early provenance unknown; Wroclaw metadata says 701-750 and same-codex relation; CLA says probably Northern Italy, 701-750. The 700-750 envelope is a documented catalogue synthesis, not local-use chronology. Original images confirm the very small fragmentary extent; no complete Canon is supplied.

evidence_checks.finding: Seventh-century lower text, c. 800 penitential overwrite, later Constance/Weingarten custody. Genre labels genuinely differ: Leonine-form, mixed Gelasian, pre-Hadrian Gregorian. Suski gives c. 650 and Ravenna? while CLA gives uncertain origin. No Canon extent or local reception follows.

evidence_checks.loci: CLA III 376 Date/Contents/Origin plus p84 sample image; Suski printed189 items 69-71 original page image; Westwell printed42 n121.

sources.inspection: Contents, physical description, origin, provenance, acquisition, license and complete TEI inspected; both S1r/S1v original images inspected. Catalogue identifies the surviving Mass formularies, one 30 x 200 mm strip, Italy/Ravenna? and first-quarter eighth-century dating based on Gamber 1958. LIMIT: Early provenance is unknown; Ravenna is low-certainty attribution. Image inspection verifies fragmentary physical extent and visible liturgical headings, not a complete transcription, independent palaeographic date, or local use.

Whole catalogue HTML and metadata inspected, including 701-750 date, current shelfmark, same-codex relation to Stockholm A 135a and public-domain image declaration. Both original image sides in the linked complete two-canvas GLAM manifest inspected. LIMIT: No Ravenna place of copying or local liturgical use is established by this record. Surviving strips do not supply the missing whole codex or a complete Eucharistic prayer.

Complete 43-page PDF acquired; title, abstract, bibliography, printed p. 189 items 69-71 and p. 196 item 145 inspected. Item 71 separates the early Gregorian lower layer of Montecassino 271 from two X/XI-century missals; item 145 identifies Stuttgart 100A and its editions. LIMIT: Catalogue descriptions are secondary evidence, not a new collation. Suski's mixed-Gelasian label for Stuttgart 100A differs from other catalogues. Listed page examples include an explicit etc., so they are not a complete denominator.

Whole journal issue acquired; article title p. 45, Milan and Montecassino entries p. 57, Stockholm and Stuttgart entries p. 65 inspected. Gives edition loci for Rotulus, fragment 100A, Stockholm-Wroclaw and Ink.15370 b om. LIMIT: A bibliographic list, not original text collation. The Wroclaw shelfmark printed Akc.1955 K/4 conflicts with the holding library's Akc.1955/3 and is retained only as an alias to resolve. Catalogue genre and origin disagreements remain open.

Previously acquired whole 944-page 1884 volume and text layer reopened; printed pp. 1-4 and 11-16 inspected, and printed p. 3 image inspected. Ceriani describes the mutilated seven-membrane roll, assigns its prayers to Advent Office use, treats Ravenna provenance as conjectural, and declares editorial spelling corrections. LIMIT: The 1884 dating claim is historical editorial judgment. The printed text expands abbreviations and corrects spellings; it is not an unaltered diplomatic transcription. Neither its Mass-book label elsewhere nor its Advent prayers establish an annual Missal.

Repository record and whole 29-page author postprint acquired; postprint p. 1 and note 2 inspected. Current shelfmark is Milan, Ambrosiana, Archivio Falco Pio di Savoia I sez.n.256(V.N.1); seventh-century recto compilation is distinguished from early-tenth-century verso letters. LIMIT: The article studies the letters, not a fresh edition of the prayers. Seven letters are ascribed to Archbishop John 905-914 and one to Sergius III 904-911; these are not dates for the recto prayers or evidence of their original altar use.

Current/former shelfmarks, VI ex (576-600), Comes Duplex contents, probable Northern Italian origin and unknown history inspected. LIMIT: The current holding-library shelfmark must be checked before merging with Usuarium 6411's Clm29270(8 alias. This is a lectionary fragment, not a Canon or anaphora witness. Ravenna attribution is unproved.

Exact shelfmarks, contents, VIII first-half (701-750) date, Northern Italian attribution, Avicenna binding provenance and script commentary inspected in the record and full 2047-row CSV export. LIMIT: The catalogue gives probable Northern Italy rather than Ravenna. This broader date differs from Manuscripta's 700-725 range; the stage retains both descriptions.

Contents, VII (601-700) date, current/former shelfmarks, uncertain origin, c. 800 penitential overwrite and Constance/Weingarten provenance inspected. Complete catalogue illustration of an opening inspected; undertext is fragmentary and difficult to read. LIMIT: The illustration is a sample, not a complete original codex. Catalogue sacramentary-type labels disagree across sources. Ravenna use and a complete Canon have not been established.

Exact lower-layer identification, VII–VIII (680-720) date, Gregorian sacramentary-fragment contents and Italian origin inspected. Provenance identifies eleventh-century Beneventan rewriting with Gregory's Dialogues. Complete catalogue illustration of p. 84 inspected. LIMIT: The sample illustration and metadata do not establish every lower-text page or whole-book content. Other reused missal strata in the same present codex must remain separate. Ravenna origin remains a scholarly question.

Whole book PDF acquired from institutional repository; title/rights page, p. 42, note 121 / PDF p. 68, 56 note 180, 58-62 and note 201 inspected. Discusses Montecassino 271 as a mass-prayer/reading book, the single Stockholm-Wroclaw codex, and the evidential limits of Gamber's Ravenna archetype hypothesis. LIMIT: Critical discussion does not independently date or locate the fragment scriptoria. No Ravenna archetype is promoted to a surviving book or historical stage. PDF figures carry separate rights.

independent_review.limits: This review independently checks the material physical, date, genre and local-use boundaries. It does not collate the missing original codices, date scripts independently, or establish a local Ravenna lineage.

remaining_gaps: No original local-use or copying-place evidence identifies these fragments as a Ravenna recension. Next: Reopen Gamber CLLA 646, 650-651, 659-660, 701 and named critical editions against full original leaves; obtain documented provenance and contemporary church-use evidence.

Complete Eucharistic-prayer extent and literal readings for 100A, the Stockholm-Wroclaw codex, Montecassino lower 2 and Ink.15370. Next: Dold 1923 pp. 10-11; Gamber 1960 pp. 455-460; Gamber 1958 pp. 111-126 and 1966 pp. 242-250; Dold 1943 pp. 1*-52*; Catella-Dell'Oro-Martini 2005 pp. 513-525. Collate surviving leaves before declaring anaphora coverage.

Archive 011 remains an origin-unassigned 186-leaf missal-calendar; no original calendar, colophon, Canon, marginal use or provenance examined. Next: Obtain public images or a detailed institutional description of archive 011's colophon, calendar including 18 August, Ordinary and Canon. Resolve any connection to the 1454 Ursian-basilica Roman-Missal report rather than assuming identity.

The Rotulus is bounded Advent prayer evidence with Office-use interpretation; sermon, diptychon, ritual and lectionary leads do not identify annual Mass books. Next: Read Benz 1967 pp. 20–31 and prayer analysis, Olivar 1969 pp. 40-58, Mohlberg appendix pp. 173-178; obtain Caronti 1922 pp. 114-118 and physical identity for Usuarium 6346. Resolve Munich current shelfmark with BSB, and Ravenna-held IRHT fragments from their original leaves.
